The Sargon Birth Legend

Item Status Why it matters
J. G. Westenholz, Legends of the Kings of Akkade: The Texts (Mesopotamian Civilizations 7; Winona Lake: Eisenbrauns, 1997), text 2 "The Birth Legend of Sargon", pp. 36–49, photos pp. 379–381 © Eisenbrauns / Penn State UP; Project MUSE says "Open Access: No" (https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/2/monograph/book/80874) The current edition: all four manuscripts (with K 7249 = CT 46 46), continuous numbering, normalization, translation, commentary. Its translation of ll. 1–14 is quoted on a blog (https://clairesulos.com/2023/05/20/the-neo-assyrian-birth-legend/, retrieved 2026-10-21) — the only modern rendering we could see; quoted briefly, with attribution, in the annotated file.
B. Lewis, The Sargon Legend: A Study of the Akkadian Text and the Tale of the Hero Who Was Exposed at Birth (ASOR Dissertation Series 4; Cambridge, MA, 1980) © ; archive.org sargonlegendstud0000lewi is lending-only (and archive.org is blocked in the cloud session) Text, translation, and the comparative study of the exposed-hero tale (Moses, Cyrus, Romulus …).
E. Jiménez, "New Fragments and Extracts of Akkadian Disputation and Fables Chiefly from Babylonian Schools", Orientalia 87 (2018), pp. 155–156 (copy and edition of BM 47449; eBL bibliography RN2877) © The school tablet with the Sargon extract: eBL's col. 4′ lines (the only ones it transliterates) belong to Jiménez's study of disputation and fable extracts, so they are probably not the legend.
A. K. Grayson, Babylonian Historical-Literary Texts (1975) p. 8 n. 11 © Mentions BM 47449.
CT 13 pls. 42–43 (King 1901), CT 46 46 (Lambert & Millard 1965) — the hand copies CT 13 is public domain, but its scans are on archive.org (blocked); CDLI line-art P365306/P365307/P365303 (cdli.earth answered 503 "temporarily offline" all day, 2026-10-21) Checking King's readings against the copies, and K 7249.
CDLI P365306, P365307, P365303 (ATF, if any) cdli.earth offline (503) on 2026-10-21 (retried 4 times) A possible newer transliteration. Retry https://cdli.earth/artifacts/365306/json.
"Slightly Alive Translations — The Birth Legend of Sargon (CT 13 42–43)", https://mostlydeadlanguages.tumblr.com/post/141852754788/ tumblr answered 502 A blogger's transliteration from the CT copies (not a scholarly edition).

Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta

Item Status
S. Cohen, Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta (PhD diss., University of Pennsylvania, 1973) ProQuest; the basis of ETCSL's composite
S. N. Kramer, Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta: A Sumerian Epic Tale of Iraq and Iran (Museum Monographs; Philadelphia: University Museum, 1952) archive.org only (blocked); old readings (rank 5)
H. L. J. Vanstiphout, Epics of Sumerian Kings: The Matter of Aratta (SBLWAW 20; Atlanta, 2003) © SBL; ETCSL's translation follows it
S. N. Kramer, "The 'Babel of Tongues': A Sumerian Version", JAOS 88 (1968) 108–111; Th. Jacobsen, "The Spell of Nudimmud", in Sha'arei Talmon (1992) 403–416; H. Vanstiphout, "Another Attempt at the 'Spell of Nudimmud'", RA 88 (1994) 135–154; B. Alster, "An Aspect of 'Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta'", RA 67 (1973) 101–110; J. Klein, "The Origin and Development of Languages on Earth: The Sumerian versus the Biblical View", in Sefer Moshe (2004) 77–92 © (journals / Festschriften); the main literature on the Nudimmud spell ↔ Gen 11. Mittermayer 2009 (open, ../Mittermayer-2009--…/) summarizes and discusses all of them (pp. 57–63 and the commentary on 134–155).
Th. Jacobsen, The Harps that Once… (1987) 275–319; J. Black et al., The Literature of Ancient Sumer (2004) 3–22 ©
